home.metaTitle: Polish Footprints: Istanbul – Polish history walks and map app
home.metaDesc: 38 places and 8 self-guided walks that trace Polish history in Istanbul: Polonezköy (Adampol), the Adam Mickiewicz Museum, envoys at the sultan's court, Roxelana, the 1939 gold and John Paul II. Stories in Polish, English and Turkish, for iPhone and iPad.
home.ogDesc: A self-guided history map of Polish Istanbul: 38 places and 8 walks, from Adampol (Polonezköy) to the Mickiewicz Museum, in Polish, English and Turkish.
home.ogAlt: The Polish Footprints app icon – a compass rose with a tulip on a blue tile crossed by a white and red sash – with the title Polish Footprints, Istanbul
home.eyebrow: iPhone and iPad · Polish, English and Turkish
home.h1: The Polish footprints of Istanbul, on foot
home.lead: A map and pocket guide to 38 places where Poles left their mark on Istanbul – from Adampol, the Polish village in the forests above the Bosphorus, to the house where Adam Mickiewicz died, the gates through which the Commonwealth's envoys rode to the sultan and the quay where Poland's gold passed through in 1939. Pick a place, read its story and walk there.
home.themesLead: Istanbul has a Polish story, and most visitors walk straight past it. More than six centuries of Polish–Turkish history, told place by place. Every place on the map belongs to one of these themes.
home.t1Body: The Polish village founded in 1842 at Prince Adam Czartoryski's wish in the forests of Beykoz: its church, its cemetery, “Aunt Zosia's House”, the memorial of Atatürk's visit and the nature park.
home.t2Body: The museum on the spot where Adam Mickiewicz died in November 1855, the church where the exiles were granted the land for Adampol, and the graves of General Langiewicz and Tadeusz Gasztowtt.
home.t3Body: Michał Czajkowski, the novelist who became Sadyk Pasha; Stanisław Chlebowski, court painter to Sultan Abdülaziz; and Wojciech Bobowski – Ali Ufkî – who grew up in the palace school of Topkapı.
home.t4Body: The inn where the Commonwealth's great embassies lodged, the Sublime Porte, the audience halls of Topkapı and the old “Polish Street” off İstiklal.
home.t5Body: Khotyn 1621 and the tomb of Osman II, the Yedikule fortress where Polish nobles were held, Kara Mustafa Pasha of Vienna 1683 and the site of the old slave market.
home.t6Body: Hürrem Sultan, wife of Süleyman the Magnificent, whom Polish tradition places in Rohatyn: her tomb, the bathhouse Sinan built for her and her first great foundation.
home.t7Title: Churches, cemeteries and John Paul II
home.t7Body: St Anthony's Basilica with its Sunday Mass in Polish, Santa Maria Draperis, the Cathedral of the Holy Spirit and the stops of John Paul II's visit in November 1979.
home.t8Body: In September 1939 the gold reserves of the Bank of Poland passed through Istanbul: from a British ship anchored off Kabataş to a train at Haydarpaşa bound for Beirut.
home.t9Body: The villagers of Polonezköy, the Polish Mass at St Anthony's and the Consulate General in Maslak, today's address of Polish diplomacy on the Bosphorus.
home.insideLead: Every place sits on the map, grouped by theme. Tap it for the story, the pictures, the people involved and a short note on visiting.
home.f1Body: Churches and cemeteries, palace gates and audience halls, a village, a museum, a railway station and a quay – each with its story, period, district, sources and a note on visiting. Where a story rests on tradition rather than documents, the text says so.
home.f2Body: From Mickiewicz's Pera to the village of Adampol, the old city of the sultans and the trail of John Paul II. Each walk is a route of numbered stops.
home.f3Body: Old maps, paintings, engravings and photographs beside views of the same places today – all freely licensed and credited.
home.f4Body: The stories and all the pictures are inside the app, so they work without mobile data. Only the street map and directions need a connection.
home.f5Title: Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
home.f5Body: Tap Directions to walk to a place, or hand a whole walk to your maps app with one button.
home.f6Title: Your location stays on your phone
home.f6Body: Distances and the “you are here” dot are worked out on the phone. No account, no ads, no tracking.
home.walksLead: Each walk links places that belong to one story. The times are rough guides for walking and looking, without museum visits.

home.faq1q: Is this a self-guided walking tour of Polish Istanbul?
home.faq1a: Yes. The eight walks are self-guided routes with numbered stops and a story at each one. You walk at your own pace, and the app hands the stops to Apple Maps or Google Maps for directions.
home.faq2q: Which places are in the app?
home.faq2a: 38 places linked to Polish history in Istanbul, for example the village of Polonezköy (Adampol) with its church and cemetery, the Adam Mickiewicz Museum, St Anthony's Basilica on İstiklal, the Sublime Porte and the audience halls of Topkapı Palace, the Yedikule fortress, the tomb and bathhouse of Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana), Haydarpaşa station, the grave of General Langiewicz and the Ecumenical Patriarchate, where John Paul II prayed in 1979.
home.faq3a: The stories and all the pictures are inside the app and work without a connection. The street map comes from OpenStreetMap and directions open in your maps app; both need mobile data or Wi-Fi.
home.faq4q: What is free, and what does the unlock include?
home.faq4a: The map, a first look at every place and two complete walks in and around Pera – “Mickiewicz's Pera” and “Sadyk Pasha and the Sultan's Painter” – are free. One purchase unlocks all 38 stories, all 8 walks, every picture, directions to every place and future content updates.
home.faq5a: No. It is a one-time purchase, with no ads and no account. On another iPhone or iPad, or after reinstalling, tap “Restore purchases” with the same Apple Account.
home.faq6a: Polish, English and Turkish – every story is written in all three. The app starts in your phone's language (English if it is none of the three), and you can switch in Settings.
home.faq7q: Do I need to be in Istanbul to use it?
home.faq7a: No. You can read the stories and plan your walks at home. Distances and the “you are here” dot appear once you are in the city and allow location access.
home.faq8a: No. There is no account, no advertising and no tracking. The app sends anonymous usage statistics that you can switch off in Settings; the privacy policy lists exactly what they contain.
home.faq9q: How do I get to Polonezköy (Adampol)?
home.faq9a: The village lies on the Asian side, in the forests of Beykoz, about 25 km from Sultanahmet as the crow flies. There is no rail or metro: the simplest way is a taxi from Kavacık or Beykoz (about 15–20 minutes). City buses also run there – check the current lines before you set off. The village itself can be walked in about two hours; weekdays are much quieter than weekends.

privacy.metaDesc: How the Polish Footprints: Istanbul app handles location, anonymous usage statistics, purchases and maps. No account, no ads, no tracking.
privacy.lead: Polish Footprints: Istanbul is built to need as little data as possible. There is no account, no advertising and no tracking. This page explains, in plain words, everything the app and this website do with data.
privacy.sum1: Your location is used only on your phone, and only while you use the app. Your coordinates are never stored or sent; the statistics only say whether the phone is in Istanbul (approximate location).
privacy.sum2: Anonymous usage statistics go to TelemetryDeck (Germany). No name, no e-mail, no search text, no coordinates. You can switch them off.
privacy.sum3: Purchases are handled by Apple. We never see your payment details.
privacy.sum4: No account, no ads, no cookies, no tracking across apps or websites.
privacy.factWhoV: Mehmet Gökhan Memik, trading as thebarnapp (sole proprietorship), Istanbul, Türkiye
privacy.whoBody: The app is published by thebarnapp, the sole proprietorship of Mehmet Gökhan Memik in Istanbul, Türkiye. He is responsible for the data processing described here. For any question or request, write to app@save-all.com.
privacy.locBody: The app never asks for your location when it starts. It asks only when you tap to see distances, and only for access while you use the app – never in the background. If you allow it, your position is used only on your phone: to show the “you are here” dot on the map and to measure the distance to each place. Your coordinates are never stored and never sent to us or to anyone else.
privacy.locBody2: The only thing derived from your location that leaves the phone is a yes/no/unknown value in the usage statistics (section 3): whether the phone is within about 30 km of central Istanbul. In the App Store privacy details this is listed as approximate location, used for analytics only, not linked to you and not used for tracking. The app works fully without location access; you can allow or withdraw it at any time in your phone's settings.
privacy.anaBody: To learn which places and features are used, the app sends anonymous usage statistics to TelemetryDeck GmbH, a privacy-focused analytics service based in Germany (EU). The statistics are short signals such as “a place page was opened” or “a walk was started in Maps”. They contain no name, no e-mail address, no search text and no location coordinates. Every value comes from a fixed list in the app; anything else is sent as “other”.
privacy.anaWhat1: Screens and features: app start (first start or not), which screen or tab is shown (map, explore, walks, settings, place, walk, preview, unlock screen, credits, privacy).
privacy.anaWhat2: Places and walks: which place or walk was opened, previewed, marked as visited or favourite, or handed to a maps app – identified by the app's own content id (for example “mickiewicz-museum”), its theme, and whether it is free or locked; for directions, which maps app was used (Apple Maps, Google Maps or the browser) and whether you went ahead or cancelled.
privacy.anaWhat3: Map and search: theme filters and the favourites filter on the map or list, the “Free: start here” hint (shown, tapped, retired), and for searches only the number of results and the length of the query in buckets (such as 3–5 letters) – never the search text.
privacy.anaWhat4: Location permission: that the map's “see distances” card was shown, and when you tap to allow location, where you tapped and how the system question ended (allowed, not allowed, location services off). Once per session, if location cannot be used, the general reason.
privacy.anaWhat5: Unlock and purchases: the unlock screen shown or closed and what opened it, a purchase started, completed, cancelled, pending or failed (with a general reason), restore requested and its result, a redeem code sheet opened, and whether a completed purchase was a real one or a test (as the App Store's own transaction record says). For a real purchase, the unlock's fixed list price in US dollars is counted so we can see sales; never your local price, store country or payment data.
privacy.anaWhat6: Settings: theme, language and maps app changed, marks cleared, “Rate the app” opened, “Share the app” used (and whether the share sheet was completed or closed – not where it was sent), and the statistics switch itself (switching off sends one last signal, then nothing more).
privacy.anaWhat7: Nothing else: no contacts, photos, files, health data, browsing history or advertising identifiers are ever read.
privacy.ctxChannel: How this copy of the app was installed: development build, TestFlight, App Store, App Review (a store copy run by Apple's reviewers) or unknown.
privacy.ctxEntitled: Whether the one-time unlock has been bought (yes/no).
privacy.ctxLang: The app's language: Polish, English, Turkish or other.
privacy.ctxTheme: The app's theme: dark, light or phone setting.
privacy.ctxIst: Whether the phone is within about 30 km of central Istanbul: yes, no or unknown. Worked out on the phone; the coordinates never leave it.
privacy.ctxCheck: For copies from the App Store: whether the copy is in fact being run by Apple's App Review, and which sign showed it – so that review sessions are not counted as real users.
privacy.ctxDiag: A short technical code from the same check (for example whether the App Store's record of this copy could be read and whether the running version is newer than the one on the App Store). No dates, no device names, no store account.
privacy.anaSdk: The TelemetryDeck software adds technical details such as the app version and build number, the iOS version, the device model and screen size, the phone's language, region and time zone, display and accessibility settings (for example dark mode or larger text), the day and hour of use and simple counters such as the number of sessions. It also sends a signal when a session starts and when a new installation is detected.
privacy.anaId: To count users rather than app starts, the analytics software uses the random identifier that iOS gives the apps of one developer on your device (not the advertising identifier). It turns it into a one-way hash on the phone before anything is sent, so TelemetryDeck receives a value that cannot be traced back to you, your device or your Apple Account. It is not linked to any other data about you and is not used for advertising or tracking across apps or websites. TelemetryDeck receives the data over an encrypted connection; like any internet server it sees the connection's IP address, and it states that it does not store it.
privacy.anaTest: Development builds, TestFlight builds and App Store copies run by Apple's App Review send their statistics marked as test data, kept apart from the statistics of the published app.
privacy.anaOpt: Open the app's Settings and switch off “Share anonymous usage statistics”. The app then sends one last signal saying that statistics were switched off, stops the analytics software and sends nothing more. The choice is saved on the phone; while it is off, the analytics software is not started at all.
privacy.anaBasis: Legal basis: our legitimate interest in understanding, in anonymous form, how the guide is used so that we can improve it (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR), with the right to object at any time through the switch above.
privacy.buyBody: The one-time unlock is sold and paid through the Apple App Store, under Apple's own terms and privacy policy. We never see your name, payment details or Apple Account. The app only receives the store's confirmation that the unlock was bought, reads from it whether it was a real purchase or a test, and remembers the unlock on your phone.
privacy.mapBody: The street map is made of map tiles loaded from OpenStreetMap's servers. Like any website, those servers see your IP address and the requested map area when they deliver a tile. Their handling is described in the OpenStreetMap Foundation privacy policy.
privacy.picBody: All pictures and stories are bundled inside the app. Viewing them sends no request anywhere.
privacy.handTitle: 7. Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
privacy.handBody: When you tap Directions or start a walk in Maps, the app opens Apple Maps, Google Maps or a web browser and passes it the destination – the place or the stops of the walk. From then on, that app handles the route under its own privacy policy (Apple, Google).
privacy.connBody: Apart from the statistics and the map, the app connects to the internet only in these cases:
privacy.conn1: App version check: when a copy from the App Store starts, it asks Apple's public App Store lookup for the version number currently on sale. The request contains only the app's store number, no data about you; Apple sees the connection's IP address. The answer helps to recognise copies run by App Review (section 3).
privacy.conn2: “Rate the app” and links: these open the App Store page or a website (for example the sources in Credits & licences) only when you tap them.
privacy.conn3: “Share the app”: opens the iPhone share sheet with a short text and a link to this website. You choose whether and where to send it; the app does not see the recipient.
privacy.deviceBody: Your language and theme, the maps app you chose, the places you mark as visited or favourite, the statistics switch, whether you have seen the “Free: start here” hint and the record that you bought the unlock are saved only on your phone. Use “Clear” in the settings or delete the app to remove them.
privacy.noTitle: 10. No accounts, no ads, no tracking
privacy.noBody: There is no sign-in and no advertising. The app does not ask for your name or e-mail, does not use the advertising identifier and does not track you across other apps or websites. We do not sell or share data.
privacy.webBody: This website uses no cookies, no analytics and no third-party scripts; its fonts are served from the site itself. Your language and theme choice are saved in your browser's local storage and never sent. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages; GitHub processes server logs, including IP addresses, as described in the GitHub privacy statement.
privacy.kidsBody: The app is a history guide for a general audience and is not directed at children. It collects no personal data from anyone, children included.
privacy.rightsBody: Depending on where you live (for example under the GDPR, the UK GDPR or Turkey's KVKK), you have the right to access, correct or delete personal data, to restrict or object to processing and to complain to a data protection authority (in Poland, the UODO). Because the statistics are anonymous, we cannot link them to you, but you can always switch them off. Write to app@save-all.com with any request.
privacy.srcBody: The pictures come from Wikimedia Commons and are in the public domain (including CC0) or under Creative Commons licences (CC BY and CC BY-SA, versions 3.0 and 4.0). Every picture shows its author, source and licence under the image, and the full list is in the app under Settings › Credits & licences. Every story lists its sources. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL). Fonts: Playfair Display and Lora, SIL Open Font License 1.1. The App Store screenshots use the photo “Polonezköy nature panorama” by Darwinek (CC BY-SA 3.0) as a background; the other backgrounds are in the public domain.
privacy.changeBody: If the app's handling of data changes, this page will be updated before the new version is released, and the effective date below will change.
support.metaDesc: Help with Polish Footprints: Istanbul: restoring the unlock, offline use, location permission, directions in Apple Maps and Google Maps, language, theme and contact.
support.lead: Something not working, or a question about a place? Write to us – every message is read and answered, in Polish, English or Turkish.
support.mailHint: Please mention your iPhone or iPad model, its iOS version and the app version (shown at the top of the app's Settings).
support.faq1q: How do I restore my purchase on a new iPhone or after reinstalling?
support.faq1a: Open Settings › Full access › Restore purchases (the button is also on the unlock screen) and use the same Apple Account you bought with. The app also checks quietly at start, so a reinstalled app usually unlocks by itself once it is online. You can enter a promotional code with Redeem code in the same place.
support.faq2q: Can my family use the unlock?
support.faq2a: Yes: the unlock supports Family Sharing, so the members of your Apple family group get it too. They open the app and tap Restore purchases.
support.faq3q: Does the app work without mobile data?
support.faq3a: Yes for the stories and pictures: they are inside the app. The street map is loaded from OpenStreetMap and needs a connection, and so do directions in your maps app; without one, the places and walks are still listed and readable.
support.faq4q: Why does the app ask for my location, and can I say no?
support.faq4a: The app asks only when you tap to see distances. Your location is used only on your phone, to show the “you are here” dot and the distance to each place, and is never stored or sent. You can say no – everything else works. To change it later: Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services › Footprints on your iPhone or iPad.
support.faq5q: How do directions work in Apple Maps and Google Maps?
support.faq5a: On a place page, tap Directions. On a walk, tap Start the walk in Maps. Google Maps takes the whole walk with all its stops. Apple Maps gives walking directions to one stop at a time: mark the stop as visited and tap again for the next one. For walks with a ferry or long distances, the app offers directions by public transport. The app asks once which maps app to use; you can change it in Settings under Navigation app.
support.faq6q: How do I turn off the usage statistics?
support.faq6a: Open Settings and switch off Share anonymous usage statistics. The statistics are anonymous anyway – the privacy policy lists exactly what they contain.
support.faq7q: How do I change the language or the dark/light theme?
support.faq7a: In Settings, choose Polski, English or Türkçe under Language, and Dark, Light or “Use phone setting” under Appearance. The app starts in your phone's language if it is Polish, English or Turkish, and in English otherwise.
support.faq8q: I found a mistake in a story. How do I report it?
support.faq8a: Thank you – corrections are very welcome! Please write to app@save-all.com with the name of the place, what is wrong and, if you can, a source. Every story lists its sources in the app, and corrections are included in the next update. New places and walks with a Polish story are welcome too.
support.faq9q: I bought the unlock, but places are still locked.
support.faq9a: Make sure the device is online and signed in to the Apple Account you bought with, then tap Restore purchases in Settings › Full access. If a payment is still pending (for example Ask to Buy), the unlock arrives once it is approved. If it still does not work, write to us.
support.faq10q: Are the opening hours in the app up to date?
support.faq10a: The app does not list fixed opening hours, because churches, museums and cemeteries change them often. Each place has a note on visiting that says what to check and where (for example the parish, the museum's website or the consulate). If something has changed, please tell us.
